quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To see better when passing a vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the middle of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This improves your view ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider lean together.
The motorcycle and rider lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle leans, but the rider stays straight.
The rider leans, but the motorcycle stays straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider lean together.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is normally best, switch to single file when turning, going through curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: Slower than during the day under the same conditions.
At the same speed as during the day under the same conditions.
Faster than during the day under the same conditions.
On the road shoulder so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than during the day under the same conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day in similar weather and traffic. It is harder to see hazards in the dark, so slower speed helps you avoid them.

questions.question: Generally, the body eliminates one drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours since drinking from the total number of drinks consumed. In this case, about four drinks would still be in the person's system.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Only use the rear brake on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists seldom hear their tire go flat. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is the usual sign of tire failure.

questions.question: Face shields and goggles:

options.text: Will likely never need to be replaced.
Will get scratches and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
Should be made of breakable materials so they break away in a crash.
Should not allow any air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will get scratches and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are plastic and will get scratches and become brittle over time. Replace them regularly for the best protection and comfort.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator discourage other drivers from sharing their lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the middle of the lane
By riding on the left side of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the middle of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the middle of your lane to fill the space on both sides of your motorcycle. This reduces room for other drivers to try to share your lane.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle sits lower with a passenger's extra weight. Ride slower, especially on curves and bumps. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, or stop. Keep a larger space cushion when carrying a passenger.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind, blind spots, and road hazards. It stops other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears. It cannot help you avoid traffic signals.

questions.question: To increase your chances of being seen at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times when riding. This is the best way to help others see you at an intersection.

questions.question: If you are riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings and your motorcycle begins to weave, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle may weave on rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is usually safe. Stay calm and ride straight at a steady speed. Do not weave side to side, as this makes the danger worse.

questions.question: When riding in fog, you should:

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use your high beams when other vehicles are near.

questions.question: When making a turn:

options.text: There is less grip available for stopping.
There is more grip available for stopping.
Stopping works the same as on a straight road.
You should never try to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less grip available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but be very careful. When your motorcycle leans to turn, less grip is available for stopping because some grip is being used for the turn.

questions.question: If taking a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel tired.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold.
Ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold.
questions.explanation: Protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain to reduce fatigue on long trips. Limit riding to no more than six hours per day. Take a rest break at least every two hours. Do not use stimulants like caffeine, because extreme fatigue follows when they wear off.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let vehicles in blind spots pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: Once a motorcycle helmet has been in a crash, it should be:
questions.explanation: Replace your helmet after any crash.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected if they are wearing:

options.text: Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely. Choose tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they do not catch on foot pegs or the road. Leather gloves or other durable material protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay next to the vehicle until the next exit, then exit.
Let the other driver handle it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if danger appears. Speed up or drop back to get away from the vehicle.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar during motorcycle acceleration?

options.text: It feels like it is falling behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. Due to its weight and inertia, it will feel like it is falling behind when you accelerate.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulatory signs are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When you are about to pass a vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you the best view of the road ahead for passing safely.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of the lane to stay away from them. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.
